title: Config-aware Invocation Sentry: Golden-set + Regression Runner for Tool/Function Calls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a config-aware evaluation runner (Invocation Sentry) that continuously measures tool/function selection accuracy and argument validation correctness against a curated golden set and live soft-matches. The runner will be triggered by: model version changes, runtime config flips (batching/kv-cache/quantization), and canary rollouts. Goals: detect quality regressions attributable to model vs serving config; produce actionable signal for rollbacks or mitigations; keep compute cost bounded with sampling/stratified selection.
acceptance_criteria: A curated golden set (>=1200 examples covering common tool selectors and edge cases) is stored in S3 + versioned in the eval catalog
Runner executes on config/model change events and produces a per-run report with: tool-selection accuracy, arg-schema-validation F1, top-10 failure clusters, delta vs baseline
Alerts created when tool-selection accuracy drops >3% absolute or arg-validation F1 drops >5% (configurable), with attribution hints to either model or config
Reports surfaced in Console (Invocations -> Regression runs) and a lightweight CSV artifact pushed to the regression dashboard for triage
Cost budget enforced: monthly compute spend cap and per-run sampling cap; canary runs run at 10% sample, full runs at up to 5k examples/day only on schedule
Integration tests (unit + e2e with a small in-memory runtime) are in CI and PR passes for the initial implementation
implementation_notes: Golden set composition: 70% high-frequency production patterns, 20% long-tail/edge-case templates, 10% synthetic adversarial examples (arg permutations)
Runner architecture: event listener (model/config change) -> sampler service -> job scheduler -> workers that call current runtime under test -> scorer/attributor -> report generator

Attribution heuristics: run baseline on pinned model+config, then run candidate; compute per-example signal (tool-change, arg-diff). If tool-change correlates with model change across >60% of failing examples, tag as model; if correlated with config (e.g., quantization, batching) then tag as config
Argument validation: use schema-aware comparator (ignores ordering for object args, tolerates formatting differences), and a soft-match threshold for near-equal numerical arguments
Privacy: all sampled inputs must be filtered for PII before storing results; no raw prompts persisted for flagged customer traffic
Rollout integration: wire to rollout service to automatically pause canaries when regressions exceed thresholds
risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives from golden set drift will cause noisy alerts — mitigated by periodic goldset refresh and soft-match logic
Attribution errors when model and config change together — mitigated by synthetic ablation runs that flip only one axis
Compute cost vs sensitivity tradeoff: larger sample sizes increase detection power but raise cost; start conservative and tune thresholds based on empirical ROC
Potential latency in detection if we rely only on scheduled full runs; immediate canary-triggered runs are prioritized for fast feedback
implementation_todo: Implement event listener for model/config change events (kafka topic: runtime-config-updates)
Scheduler: add canary sampling mode + full-run cron
Worker binary: call runtime via same API used by customers and capture response metadata
Scorer: implement tool-selection and arg-schema comparators and soft-match rules
Report: generate HTML + JSON summary and push CSV to dashboard storage
Add CI e2e harness with in-memory runtime and mocked change events
